content:
Looking at the folds: the first fold (vertical line) pairs the left and right halves, the second fold (horizontal line) pairs top and bottom, and the third fold (diagonal) creates a triangle that is 1/8 of the octagon, whose vertical edge lies on the first fold line and whose top corner is a vertex of the octagon on the vertical axis.

Cutting off that top corner perpendicular to the vertical edge removes a small triangle at that vertex. Unfolding the third fold mirrors this cut to the vertex on the horizontal axis (left vertex); unfolding the second fold mirrors both cuts to the bottom and right vertices; unfolding the first fold completes each cut symmetrically.

So the cuts appear exactly at the four vertices on the vertical and horizontal axes (top, bottom, left, right), while the four diagonal vertices remain untouched. The result is a shape with four long flat sides (top, bottom, left, right) and four small chamfered diagonal corners — exactly picture C.

\boxed{C}
